parts.label: (a)
parts.text:

| energy change | always positive | always negative | either negative or positive |

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Define, in words, the term enthalpy change of solution.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The following enthalpy changes are given.

| enthalpy change | value/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| standard enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}$, for $\text{K}_3\text{PO}_4\text{(s)}$ | $-2035$ |
| standard enthalpy change, $\Delta H^{\ominus}$, for $\text{P(s)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{PO}_4^{3-}\text{(aq)}$ | $-1284$ |
| standard enthalpy change, $\Delta H^{\ominus}$, for $\text{K(s)} \rightarrow \text{K}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{e}^-$ | $-251$ |

Determine the standard enthalpy change of solution of potassium phosphate, $\text{K}_3\text{PO}_4\text{(s)}$. It may be helpful to draw a labelled energy cycle.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Some lattice energy values are shown in the table.

| compound | lattice energy value/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{CaBr}_2\text{(s)}$ | $-2176$ |
| $\text{KBr(s)}$ | $-679$ |

Suggest an explanation for why $\Delta H_{\text{latt}}^{\ominus}$ $\text{CaBr}_2$ is more exothermic than $\Delta H_{\text{latt}}^{\ominus}$ $\text{KBr}$.

parts.label: (e)
(e)(i)
parts.text: Write the equation that relates $\Delta G^{\ominus}$ to $\Delta H^{\ominus}$ and $\Delta S^{\ominus}$.
